anchor: some by-paths have an enticement
note: Enticement: attraction, a pull toward something tempting.

anchor: the original introduction from China into Europe of gunpowder
note: Gunpowder, an explosive of saltpetre, charcoal, and sulphur, altered the whole art of war after it reached Europe.

anchor: scouted by no few of the knights as a base implement
note: Scouted: rejected with scorn. Base: low, unworthy.

anchor: good enough peradventure for weavers too craven
note: Peradventure: perhaps. Craven: cowardly, too timid to fight in the open.

anchor: knightly valor, tho’ shorn of its blazonry
note: Blazonry: the display of coats of arms and show. Valor kept going without the show.

anchor: naval magnates as Don John of Austria
note: Don John of Austria led the Christian fleet that defeated the Turks at the Battle of Lepanto in 1571.

anchor: Doria
note: Andrea Doria (1466 to 1560) was a Genoese soldier of fortune who became a famous admiral.

anchor: Van Tromp
note: Tromp is the name of two famous Dutch admirals, a father and son of the 1600s.

anchor: Jean Bart
note: Jean Bart was a French naval commander from Dunkirk who rose from fisherman’s son to hero in the wars of Louis XIV.

anchor: the American Decaturs of 1812
note: Stephen Decatur was an American naval officer, famous for burning the captured frigate Philadelphia at Tripoli in 1804 and for fighting in the War of 1812.

anchor: their wooden walls
note: Wooden walls: the old name for wooden warships as England’s defense.

anchor: a poetic reproach, softened by its picturesqueness
note: Picturesqueness: beauty fit for a picture.

anchor: to the Monitors and yet mightier hulls of the European ironclads
note: Ironclads were steam warships armored with iron plates. Monitors were an American type with a revolving gun turret.

anchor: to the extent of iconoclasm
note: Iconoclasm: attacking cherished beliefs and traditions. The modern critic is willing to smash old idols.

anchor: these martial utilitarians
note: Utilitarians: people who judge things by their practical usefulness.

anchor: Nelson’s ornate publication of his person in battle
note: At Trafalgar Nelson walked the quarter deck of the Victory and was struck by a musket shot from the French ship Redoubtable that broke his spine.
source: Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th ed. (1911), “Nelson, Horatio Nelson, Viscount”, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Nelson%2C_Horatio_Nelson%2C_Viscount

anchor: savored of foolhardiness and vanity
note: Foolhardiness: reckless daring that ignores danger.

anchor: his sagacious dying injunctions overruled
note: Sagacious: wise. Injunctions: orders. Nelson’s dying order to anchor was reportedly not followed after the battle.

anchor: the Benthamites of war
note: Benthamites were followers of Jeremy Bentham, a philosopher who judged laws and acts by their usefulness.

anchor: the might-have-been is but boggy ground to build on
note: Boggy ground cannot hold a building. Melville says guessing about what might have happened is not reliable.

anchor: buoying the deadly way and mapping it out, as at Copenhagen
note: Before Copenhagen in 1801, boats of the British fleet sounded the channel so that Nelson could bring his ships through.

anchor: few commanders have been so painstakingly circumspect
note: Circumspect: careful, looking at all possible consequences.

anchor: If the name Wellington is not so much of a trumpet to the blood
note: Wellington defeated Napoleon at Waterloo in 1815. Melville says his name stirs the blood less than Nelson’s.
source: Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th ed. (1911), “Wellington, Arthur Wellesley, 1st Duke of”, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Wellington%2C_Arthur_Wellesley%2C_1st_Duke_of

anchor: Alfred in his funeral ode on the victor of Waterloo
note: Alfred Tennyson wrote the Ode on the Death of the Duke of Wellington, published in 1852.
source: Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th ed. (1911), “Tennyson, Alfred Tennyson, 1st Baron”, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Tennyson%2C_Alfred_Tennyson%2C_1st_Baron

anchor: the jewelled vouchers of his own shining deeds
note: Vouchers: proofs or evidence. Nelson’s decorations were jewelled proofs of his achievements.

anchor: affectation and fustian
note: Affectation: false show. Fustian: pompous, empty language.
